thread.title: Did the Bucs make the right move by cutting Doug Martin?

author: wpsuperfanboy.com
title: Did the Bucs make the right move by cutting Doug Martin?
text:
Did the Bucs make the right move by cutting Doug Martin?
Martin could latch on elsewhere, because he's just 29 years old and there's the siren song of those two huge seasons in his past.
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers ' offseason purge of high-priced and underperforming veterans began on Tuesday, with the team announcing it released running back Doug Martin .
With Martin's release, the Bucs create $6.75M in cap space.
That only proved to cost the Buccaneers more money, as Martin would ink a five-year deal worth over $35 million before the 2016 National Football League season.

A first-round pick by the Buccaneers in 2012, Martin emerged on the scene looking like a running back that could be in the conversation at the top of the league. He was named to the Pro Bowl twice during his career with the Bucs. He ranked fourth in rushing yards and rushing touchdowns and fifth in scrimmage yards in franchise history. He rushed for more than 1,400 yards.
In 2016, Martin was suspended for four games in violation of the NFL's substance abuse policy, testing positive for Adderall.
Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times first reported the move. The next two seasons were less successful - Martin played just 17 games between 2013-14 while battling various injuries. He earned his second Pro Bowl selection. As a result of his resurgence, Martin inked a five-year, $35.75 million extension with the Bucs.
Martin has rushed for less than 500 yards in four of his last five seasons.
